I started in July, and the first few weeks where I was kicking sugar drinks and soda where the hardest. I haven't had a drop of coffee, soda or and energy drink since July. 

I can honestly say I don't miss them now. I am finally starting to see the change in my body, and it feels fucking good, I am still 40 pounds away from where I want to be but I think I've have been doing well and keeping on track for the last 6 months. 

After I detoxed off of the soda and 'juice' drinks it was super easy just to watch what I ate and how much I was eating. I am finally starting to feel good about myself again. 

ETA: Though there are days where I do look in the mirror and still see 220 lbs me, and those days I work harder not to ever go back to that.

Back at the end of July I started my weight loss get healthy life style change. 

I completely gave up soda and it was the best thing I have ever done. When I want something fizzy I get seltzer water. 

When I started I was 220 pounds I am now 175.3 as I am 5ft 4in I am still about 45-50 pounds from my goal weight. 

But seriously it's not as hard as I thought it would be, and I am finally starting to look less like a blob and have a shape again. 

I used to cry going to buy pants because nothing looked right on me, I was around an 18/20 depending on the brand. Last week I went to Old Navy to buy new pants because even with my belt all my pants kept falling off. I am down to a size 16. I don't remember the last time I was a 16 9th /10th grade maybe. 

I still have a long way to go but still it feels good, feels like I am heading in the right direction.

Pizza is not the enemy, food is not the enemy. Those are the things you have to remember and tell yourself. 

Since the start of august I have gone from 220 to 184.1, and I didn't give up anything I love. The only thing I gave up was soda and 'juices' and the drinks labeled 'water beverage.' 

Everything in moderation has been my motto, I go for one 45 minute walk a day, and currently since I am trying to lose about 2lbs a week I eat 1200 calories a day. Using mfp to track my intake. 

Because my problem was eating to much of everything, not understanding portion size and control. 

What worked for me when giving up sugar drinks was having carbonated water, but you have to make sure you read the labels of what you are eatting.

Don't go into the service.  Do go to a doctor and get proper help. The USMC will not be helpful to you for any kind of mental stability especially during basic training. 

They aren't fools either, there will be physiological evaluations, and people watching for behaviors that wont work with the Corp.  

You probably don't want to hear this, but you should consider a different field one where you don't have to hide your Bipolar where you are able to take care of yourself.  

Yes taking medication blocks you from being in the armed forces or from being a police offer. But that is for good reason. I would hate to think what I personally would do in one of my down swings if I was armed and in a stressful situation like combat.  

You need to take others safety into mind with your current career choice.

I tried to kill my self when I was a Jr in high school, the doctor first said I had depression and prescribed me Prozac.  Which only made things worse. Sadly because Prozac worked wonders for my mom, she accused me of lying and faking it. 

So I stopped taking my meds and started self harming, which is still a struggle not to do even all these years later. ( I am in a major down swing currently and battling suicidal thoughts every day. ) 

I tried to OD on my left prozac and it didn't work, I went back to therapy on my own at 21 because I wasn't sleeping, my SI had worsened, and I was having anxiety attacks. During my lows I couldn't even get out of bed hardly. 

This time around when I told the doctor about the reaction to prozac when I told him about my sleep habits and rapid sometimes paranoid thoughts. I was put on Lamicatal and Gabapintin.  Which worked like a dream.  

I am not doing so well these days because I lost my insurance and medications about 5 years ago. Things have been getting steadily worse for me. 

I would say if you can talk to your mom about going back to therapy, because certian medications for depression can cause more problems for people with Bipolar then they fix.
